newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says French intolerance rising, hits image.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says French intolerance rising, hits image.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, in a veiled attack on the extreme-right National Front, said the "forces of intolerance" were gaining in France and tarnishing the country's image abroad.
He cautioned that unbridled intolerance had led in history to "the worst catastrophes" such as Nazism.

"Tolerance today is under threat. The forces of intolerance are growing today in our country. You only have to read the foreign press to see what a bad image it gives of France," he said during a two-hour interview with France 2 television.
"This intolerance is so alien to our traditions," he said.
Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front Party captured its fourth town hall in a municipal election in the southern town of Vitrolles last month. Le Pen wants to send home three million immigrants.

Chirac, in a broadcast largely aimed at reassuring young people hit by high unemployment, said he wanted the young to know that "nothing is as important as the outstretched hand, the kindly look, help, generosity."
"All forms of intolerance have always in the history of all countries led to the worst catastrophes, authoritarian regimes, Nazism, etc," he said, without naming the National Front.
He said young people should lead a fight for tolerance in France. "A great nation is one that knows how to integrate all its children," he said.
Le Pen won 15 percent of the vote in 1995 presidential elections won by Chirac and hopes that legislative elections in early 1998 will confirm his party as a major force.
